subject: Realtime API: cascading retries causing p99 / 429 spike — urgent
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily@cartoanalytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Realtime API: p99 timeout & 429 surge impacting live product

Hi Karthik,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95/p99 latencies this morning on our live Realtime feature (US region). Errors are primarily 429 + client timeouts; users are reporting intermittent hangs. Attached a short error sample and timestamps.

Key impact:
- 10% of production calls in the last 30m returned 429
- p99 for token generation jumped from ~450ms to 3.2s
- Our frontend retries aggressively which appears to amplify the failure window

This is customer-facing and we're getting inbound from account owners. Can you escalate and tell us what immediate steps Redwood can take to stabilize? We need something within the next 2–4 hours.

Attachments: carto_error_snippets.log

Thanks,
Emily Zhao
Head of Platform Ops — Carto Analytics
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Emily Zhao <emily@cartoanalytics.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-30T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime API: p99 timeout & 429 surge impacting live product

Emily — thanks for the heads-up and the log snippet. I’m escalating this to our on-call infra/ops and CS immediately. Short plan:

1) Triage now (sean) to identify amplification patterns and short-term mitigation.
2) Monica to coordinate customer comms and any credit/SLA asks.
3) I'll loop in leadership if we need capacity/priority escalation.

Request from our side: can you confirm whether your client does exponential backoff + jitter for 429s? If not, that appears to be making the spike worse.

I’ll follow up within 30 minutes with a proposed immediate mitigation (hotfix + config change) and a timeline.

Attachments: first-pass-triage.txt

—
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-30T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime API: p99 timeout & 429 surge impacting live product — initial findings

Quick technical summary from the triage:

- Root cause appears to be a retry-amplification loop. Carto’s SDK retried on 429s aggressively (no jitter, fixed backoff), which created synchronized bursts that filled our request queues and drove CPU spikes on the inference pool.
- Observed queue dwell time increase correlates with p99 jumps. Once queues lengthen, KV cache warm paths get evicted and per-token time rises.
- We are returning 429s without a consistent Retry-After header in some edge cases; that also causes client retries to fire immediately.

Immediate mitigations we can deploy (recommended order):
1) Push an edge configuration to send Retry-After on 429s for affected routes (30m deploy window).
2) Apply a temporary per-api-key soft limit + token-bucket override for Carto to smooth their burst (requires support approval — ~1h).
3) Recommend Carto update SDK to exponential backoff + jitter (we’ll provide exact guidance).
4) If traffic remains unstable, enable constrained dedicated capacity for their key for 24–48h while we stabilize (ops/infra decision).

I’ve created INF-2145 and captured traces for the window. See Grafana: https://grafana.redwood-inference.internal/d/hosted/p99-spike?view=carto and attached screenshots + logs.

Attachments: grafana-p99-spike.png, retry-trace-logs.txt

—
Sean Gallagher
SRE — Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Emily Zhao <emily@cartoanalytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime API: p99 timeout & 429 surge impacting live product — Redwood action plan

Emily — thanks again and sorry for the disruption. We are treating this as an active incident and here are immediate actions we are taking:

1) Edge change to add consistent Retry-After on 429s — deploy in 30–45 minutes.
2) Temporary soft-rate smoothing on your API key to flatten bursts (we’ll coordinate the exact threshold) — ~1 hour.
3) Engineering to share recommended SDK backoff config (we’ll send a snippet you can apply today).
4) Follow-up post-mortem with timeline and mitigation notes within 48 hours.

We can also provision a short-lived isolated capacity pool if your traffic pattern requires guaranteed throughput while you roll out client fixes — that takes longer but we can have a plan in 24 hours.

If acceptable, can we schedule a 30-minute call in the next 90 minutes so Sean/Eng and I can walk through the changes and get your confirmation for the rate smoothing? Also, please confirm procurement contact if we need to spin up dedicated capacity quickly.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Emily Zhao <emily@cartoanalytics.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ops@cartoanalytics.com, procurement@cartoanalytics.com

Subject: Re: Realtime API: p99 timeout & 429 surge impacting live product — RE: action plan

Thanks Monica — we’re good with the edge change and temporary smoothing. Please proceed.

Notes from our side:
- Confirmed their SDK currently does fixed 1s retry every attempt (no jitter). We’ll push an emergency client change as well.
- Procurement contact is procurement@cartoanalytics.com — they’re prepared to expedite a short-term addendum if needed.

We’d like weekly exec summaries for the next month and visibility on any credits tied to uptime impact; happy to take a quick sync now.

Emily
